24530-on-the-tree-top.creator: Unknown
24530-on-the-tree-top.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. A miller had a daughter, And lovely, too, she was; Her step was light, her smile was bright, Her eyes were gray as glass. (So Chaucer loved to write of eyes In which that nameless azure lies So like shoal-water in its hue, Though all too crystal clear for blue.

arxiv-1509-04215.title: Superadiabatic Controlled Evolutions and Universal Quantum Computation
arxiv-1509-04215.creator: Alan C. Santos, Marcelo S. Sarandy
arxiv-1509-04215.description: Abstract Adiabatic state engineering is a powerful technique in quantum information and quantum control. However, its performance is limited by the adiabatic theorem of quantum mechanics. In this scenario, shortcuts to adiabaticity, such as provided by the superadiabatic theory, constitute a valuable tool to speed up the adiabatic quantum behavior.

arxiv-2107-14305.title: Novel wall-crossing behaviour in rank one 𝒩 = 𝟐 ∗ \bm{{\mathcal{N}}=2^{*}} gauge theory
arxiv-2107-14305.creator: Philipp Rüter, Richard J. Szabo
arxiv-2107-14305.description: Abstract We study the BPS spectrum of four-dimensional 𝒩 = 2 {\mathcal{N}}=2 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory with gauge group S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) SU(2) and a massive adjoint hypermultiplet, which has an extremely intricate structure with infinite spectrum in all chambers of its Coulomb moduli space, and is not well understood.

arxiv-2109-07848.title: The Language Model Understood the Prompt was Ambiguous: Probing Syntactic Uncertainty Through Generation
arxiv-2109-07848.creator: Laura Aina, Tal Linzen
arxiv-2109-07848.description: Abstract Temporary syntactic ambiguities arise when the beginning of a sentence is compatible with multiple syntactic analyses. We inspect to which extent neural language models (LMs) exhibit uncertainty over such analyses when processing temporarily ambiguous inputs, and how that uncertainty is modulated by disambiguating cues.

arxiv-2201-12089.title: Label uncertainty-guided multi-stream model for disease screening
arxiv-2201-12089.creator: Chi Liu, Zongyuan Ge, Mingguang He, Xiaotong Han \sthanks indicates the corresponding author. Email: lh.201205@aliyun.com
arxiv-2201-12089.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Chi Liu, Zongyuan Ge, Mingguang He, Xiaotong Han \sthanks indicates the corresponding author. Email: lh.201205@aliyun.com. The annotation of disease severity for medical image datasets often relies on collaborative decisions from multiple human graders. The intra-observer variability derived from individual differences always persists in this process, yet the influence is often underestimated. In this paper, we cast the intra-observer variability as an uncertainty problem and incorporate the label uncertainty information as guidance into the disease screening model to improve the final decision.

arxiv-2303-13742.title: Dead-time optimization to increase secure distance range in prepare and measure quantum key distribution protocols
arxiv-2303-13742.creator: Carlos Wiechers, Xóchitl Sánchez-Lozano, Rafael Gómez-Medina, Mariana Salado-Mejía, J.L. Lucio
arxiv-2303-13742.description: Abstract Afterpulsing is a factor limiting the distance over which discrete-variable quantum key distribution systems are secure, and a common feature in single-photon detectors. The relevance of this phenomenon stems from its stochastic, self-interacting nature and the fact that its rate rises with the number of avalanche events, which increases the quantum bit error rate.

arxiv-2401-06770.title: Random trees with local catastrophes: the Brownian case
arxiv-2401-06770.creator: Ariane Carrance, Jérôme Casse, and Nicolas Curien
arxiv-2401-06770.description: Abstract We introduce and study a model of plane random trees generalizing the famous Bienaymé–Galton–Watson model but where births and deaths are locally correlated. More precisely, given a random variable ( B , H ) (B,H) with values in { 1 , 2 , 3 , … } 2 \{1,2,3,...

arxiv-2402-18208.title: Shorts on the Rise: Assessing the Effects of YouTube Shorts on Long-Form Video Content
arxiv-2402-18208.creator: Prajit T. Rajendran, Kevin Creusy, Vivien Garnes
arxiv-2402-18208.description: Abstract Short form content has permeated into the video creator space over the past few years, led by industry leading products such as TikTok, YouTube Shorts and Instagram Reels. YouTube in particular was previously synonymous with being the main hub for long form video content consumption.

arxiv-2504-01645.title: How to write competitive proposals and job applications
arxiv-2504-01645.creator: Johan H. Knapen, Henri M.J. Boffin, Nushkia Chamba, Natashya Chamba
arxiv-2504-01645.description: Abstract Writing proposals and job applications is arguably one of the most important tasks in the career of a scientist. The proposed ideas must be scientifically compelling, but how a proposal is planned, written, and presented can make an enormous difference. This Perspective is the third in a series aimed at training the writing skills of professional astronomers.

arxiv-2507-11874.title: Fully strange tetraquark states via QCD sum rules
arxiv-2507-11874.creator: Bing-Dong Wan 1,2 and Ji-Chong Yang 1,2
arxiv-2507-11874.description: Abstract In this paper, we have systematically explored the mass spectrum of fully strange tetraquark candidates within the framework of QCD sum rules, focusing on states with quantum numbers J P ​ C = 0 + ⁣ + J^{PC}=0^{++} , 0 − ⁣ + 0^{-+} , 0 − ⁣ − 0^{--} , 1 − ⁣ − 1^{--} , 1 +

arxiv-2509-22489.title: Passive Learning of Lattice Automata from Recurrent Neural Networks
arxiv-2509-22489.creator: Jaouhar Slimi, Tristan Le Gall, Augustin Lemesle
arxiv-2509-22489.description: Abstract We present a passive automata learning algorithm that can extract automata from recurrent networks with very large or even infinite alphabets. Our method combines overapproximations from the field of Abstract Interpretation and passive automata learning from the field of Grammatical Inference.

arxiv-2602-24289.title: Mode Seeking meets Mean Seeking for Fast Long Video Generation
arxiv-2602-24289.creator: Shengqu Cai, Weili Nie, Chao Liu, Julius Berner, Lvmin Zhang, Nanye Ma, Hansheng Chen, Maneesh Agrawala, Leonidas Guibas, Gordon Wetzstein, Arash Vahdat
arxiv-2602-24289.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Shengqu Cai, Weili Nie, Chao Liu, Julius Berner, Lvmin Zhang, Nanye Ma, Hansheng Chen, Maneesh Agrawala, Leonidas Guibas, Gordon Wetzstein, Arash Vahdat. Scaling video generation from seconds to minutes faces a critical bottleneck: while short-video data is abundant and high-fidelity, coherent long-form data is scarce and limited to narrow domains. To address this, we propose a training paradigm where Mode Seeking meets Mean Seeking, decoupling local fidelity from long-term coherence based on a unified representation via a Decoupled Diffusion Transformer ( Wang et al.

pmc-11860367.title: Early language intervention and IQ of children with non-syndromic orofacial clefts
pmc-11860367.creator: K A Sándor-Bajusz, E Molnár, T Dergez, K Hadzsiev, A Vástyán, G Csábi
pmc-11860367.description: Introduction Children with non-syndromic orofacial clefts are at higher risk for developmental difficulties. Speech and language as commonly affected developmental domains in these children.ObjectivesThe aim of the current study was to explore the effects of early interventions for speech and language on later cognitive outcomes in this patient population.

pmc-12410604.title: Cultural models within general practice/family medicine training: a scoping review protocol
pmc-12410604.creator: Lisa Collins, Helen Reid, Hinemoa Elder, Grainne Kearney
pmc-12410604.description: AbstractIntroductionCultural competency, cultural safety, cultural humility and transcultural care have developed as frameworks to better equip medical professionals towards a more culturally appropriate healthcare system. The aim of this scoping review is to map the use of these cultural models within general practice/general practitioner (GP) training.

pmc-12469617.title: Development of a Comprehensive Lesion Severity Classification Model for Largemouth Bass (Micropterus salmoides) Ranavirus (LMBV) Based on Machine Vision
pmc-12469617.creator: Hui Sun, Jixiang Hua, Yifan Tao, Ziying Yang, Taide Zhu, Siqi Lu, Wen Wang, Yalun Dong, Linbing Zhang, Jixiang He, Jie He, Jun Qiang, Antonino Germana
pmc-12469617.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study presents the development of a quantitative evaluation method utilizing machine vision technology to characterize the extent of body surface damage in largemouth bass (Micropterus salmoides) infected with largemouth bass ranavirus (LMBV). High-resolution, multi-angle images (6000 × 4000 pixels) of the body surface from 239 infected specimens were acquired at a fixed distance of 40 cm using a SONY ILCE-7RM3 digital camera within a GODOX-LST60 softbox.

pmc-12537622.title: Does obesity impact on weaning from invasive ventilation: a secondary analysis of the WEAN SAFE study
pmc-12537622.creator: Alison Bell, Akira Kuriyama, Omid Khazaei, Bairbre A. McNicholas, Tài Pham, Leo Heunks, Giacomo Bellani, Laurent Brochard, Andrew J. Simpkin, John G. Laffey
pmc-12537622.description: ObjectiveTo understand the impact of obesity on outcomes of weaning from invasive mechanical ventilation (MV).MethodsThe study population consisted of patients enrolled in the WEAN SAFE study. We defined 4 groups based on body mass index (BMI), namely: Normal weight (BMI 18.5–24.9 kg/m²), Overweight (BMI 25–29.9 kg/m²), Obesity Class I (BMI 30–34.

pmc-12706053.title: Improving nitrogen use efficiency in rice by estimating leaf nitrogen content with near-infrared spectroscopy and chemometric modeling
pmc-12706053.creator: Audberto Quiroga-Mosquera, Mariana Santos-Rivera, Diego Guzmán-Prada, Jorge Casas, Manabu Ishitani, Michael Gomez Selvaraj
pmc-12706053.description: Accurate nitrogen management in rice (Oryza sativa L.) is essential for optimizing both crop productivity and environmental sustainability. This study evaluated the potential of Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (NIRS) combined with chemometric modeling to classify leaf nitrogen content (LNC) in five rice genotypes (Nerica, Rufipogon, IR64, Ciherang, and Curinga) subjected to five nitrogen fertilization levels (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%).

pmc-12744864.title: Development of a Nomogram for Predicting Multiple Organ Dysfunction in Acute Pancreatitis
pmc-12744864.creator: Zongyuan Che, Xuchen Zhao, Wei Xue, Zhiyao Wang, Congzhong Hu, Yulin Feng, Ruijun Ru, Yanzhang Tian, Shaojian Mo
pmc-12744864.description: BackgroundMultiple Organ Dysfunction Syndrome (MODS) is a lethal complication of acute pancreatitis (AP), making early identification of high-risk patients crucial for improving outcomes.AimTo develop and validate a clinically applicable nomogram for predicting MODS risk in acute pancreatitis patients based on clinical and laboratory variables collected within the first 24 hours of admission.

pmc-12865965.title: Harmonizing self-reported and free text medication data: a reproducible pipeline for gerontological research
pmc-12865965.creator: Ramkrishna K. Singh, Chen Chen, Semere Bekena, David C. Brown, Kaylin Taylor, Matthew Blake, Yiqi Zhu, Kebede Beyene, David B. Carr, Ganesh M. Babulal
pmc-12865965.description: BackgroundSelf-reported medication data collected as free text in gerontological and dementia research is often unstructured with inconsistent formatting. These circumstances pose a challenge for standardization and classification when preparing effective, reproducible analyses. Spelling variations, naming conventions, and reporting drug combinations can hinder mapping to standard pharmacologic vocabularies and compromise medication exposure assessments.

pmc-12998364.title: Prognostic Value of the ROX Index for Mortality in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study Using the MIMIC-IV Database
pmc-12998364.creator: Kai Liu, Zehui Fu, Dahang Luo, Hua Xiao, Qiaobin Wu
pmc-12998364.description: ObjectiveWhile the ROX index has been extensively studied in acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, its prognostic value in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between the ROX index and mortality in critically ill COPD patients.

pmc-13272513.title: The role of IL-6 -174C/G polymorphism in hepatitis B virus infection: a genetic association study
pmc-13272513.creator: Nawar B. Abdulsahib, Ahmed S. Khalaf, Maryam Dhary, Ragheed H. Yousif, Ghassan M. Sulaiman, Hamdoon A. Mohammed, Majid S. Jabir, Khaled Haidar, Akram B. Sultan
pmc-13272513.description: The development of the disease after infection with the hepatitis B virus (HBV) is linked to single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). SNPs' involvement in patients' persistent HBV infection is still unknown, though. Thus, the purpose of the current study was to assess the IL-6174C/G polymorphism in hepatitis B-infected Iraqi patients.

pmc-13283290.title: Mapping intratumor heterogeneity across layers for advancing immunotherapy
pmc-13283290.creator: Jean-Christophe Marine, Osnat Bartok, Shira Sagie, Pietro Paolo Vitiello, Alberto Bardelli, Chen Weller, Tian-Gen Chang, Claudia Tonelli, Stefani Spranger, Eytan Ruppin, Yardena Samuels
pmc-13283290.description: SUMMARYIntratumor heterogeneity (ITH) encompasses genetic, epigenetic, transcriptional, proteomic, and immunopeptidomic diversity. Beyond genetic heterogeneity, it is increasingly clear that non-mutational heterogeneity and plasticity generate dynamic cancer cell states with distinct immune visibility. These layers of complexity converge on the immunopeptidome, the repertoire of peptides displayed by major histocompatibility complex molecules through which tumor cells are surveyed by T cells.

pmc-13333324.title: Hemodynamics Beyond Ischemic Zone Underlies Early Neurological Deterioration in Minor Stroke with Large Vessel Occlusion
pmc-13333324.creator: Zhijiao He, Lan Hong, Tingyu Yi, Xinru Wang, Juehua Zhu, Weijie Chen, Siyuan Li, Anqi Zhang, Nan Cao, Yifeng Ling, Guangjian Zhao, Dan Li, Ying Guo, Meihua Wu, Guozhi Lu, Ziran Wang, Danhong Wu, Qi Fang, Wenhuo Chen, Qiang Dong, Jean-Claude Baron, Xin Cheng, CHABLIS Collaboration
pmc-13333324.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Early neurological deterioration (END) occurs in a substantial proportion of minor stroke patients with large vessel occlusion or severe stenosis (LVO/SS) and is a strong predictor of poor outcome, yet its underlying mechanisms remain debated. The cerebral blood volume (CBV) index is defined as the ratio of the mean CBV in the hypoperfusion (Tmax>6s) region to the mean CBV in the normal brain tissue, incorporating hemodynamics beyond the ischemic zone into its calculation.

pmc-13339098.title: The Hidden Burden of Hemifacial Spasm: A Systematic Review of Non‐Motor Symptoms
pmc-13339098.creator: Miriam Carvalho Soares, Jacy Bezerra Parmera, Pedro Augusto Sampaio Rocha‐Filho
pmc-13339098.description: BackgroundHemifacial spasm (HFS) is a chronic neurological disorder characterized by involuntary contractions of facial muscles. Traditionally regarded as a motor condition, HFS encompasses a spectrum of non‐motor symptoms that are often overlooked but significantly affect patients’ quality of life.ObjectivesThis systematic review aimed to synthesize current evidence on the prevalence and clinical relevance of non‐motor manifestations in HFS.

pmc-13357472.title: Evaluating reasoning models for therapy recommendations in gastrointestinal stromal tumors: expert and LLM-based evaluations of OpenAI o1 and DeepSeek-R1
pmc-13357472.creator: Melissa Harbrücker, Franka Menge, Arshia Taebi, Dominik Nörenberg, Tobias Speer, Christoph Reißfelder, Peter Hohenberger, Jens Jakob, Chengpeng Li, Cui Yang
pmc-13357472.description: PurposeThis study aims to evaluate two advanced reasoning LLMs in generating treatment recommendations for real-world gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) cases and assess their concordance with multidisciplinary team (MDT) decisions at a certified tertiary sarcoma center.MethodsSixty-five real-world GIST cases from a tertiary sarcoma center were used to compare two advanced reasoning models—OpenAI o1 and DeepSeek-R1.

pmc-13368539.title: The relationship between disability and quality of life among older adults: the roles of sleep, depression, and living arrangements
pmc-13368539.creator: Jing Zhu, Zhiqiang Feng, Zhongming Chen, Lin Guo, Chengxin Fan, Chunxiao Yang, Zixuan Zhao, Xingang Sang, Lingzhong Xu, Wenqiang Yin
pmc-13368539.description: BackgroundThe acceleration of population aging, especially in China, has led to a rapid growth in the number of older adults living with disabilities, posing significant challenges to public health and quality of life (QoL). From the perspective of the biopsychosocial framework, the adverse impact of disability (a biological and functional factor) on QoL has been well documented.

pmc-13389761.title: Volume not the defining metric: Dosimetric benefits of adding supplemental interstitial needles for small volume cervical tumors
pmc-13389761.creator: Emily Smith, Nicholas Ngo, Thomas Niedermayr, Elizabeth Kidd
pmc-13389761.description: PurposeIn brachytherapy for cervical cancer, previous data have demonstrated improved local control with adding supplementary interstitial needles for cervical tumors > 30 cm3 and increased D90 to high-risk clinical target volume (HR-CTV) without increasing dose to adjacent normal tissues. Therefore, needles are more routinely added for larger volume tumors.
